facts.statement: The genus Litargosuchus was described by researchers Jim Clark and Hans-Dieter Sues in 2002.
facts.quote: authority: Clark and Sues 2002

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Litargosuchus leptorhynchus.
facts.quote: type_species: L. leptorhynchus

facts.statement: Litargosuchus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic

facts.statement: Litargosuchus is classified as a sphenosuchian crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Litargosuchus is a sphenosuchian crocodylomorph

facts.statement: This animal was a basal member of the crocodylomorph clade found in Early Jurassic South Africa.
facts.quote: basal member of the crocodylomorph clade from the Early Jurassic of South Africa

facts.statement: The species name leptorhynchus refers to the animal's gracile snout.
facts.quote: its species name leptorhynchus refers to its gracile snout

facts.statement: Litargosuchus fossils are found exclusively in the upper Elliot Formation in South Africa.
facts.quote: Litargosuchus, along with all of South Africa's crocodylomorph taxa, are confined to the upper Elliot Formation (UEF) in South Africa

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was discovered in 1988 by James Kitching at Eagles Crag near Barkly East in the Eastern Cape.
facts.quote: In 1988 James Kitching found the holotype fossil of Litargosuchus in a field expedition in Eagles Crag, a farm near Barkly East in the Eastern Cape

facts.statement: The original discovery included a near-complete skull, mandible, and several postcranial bones.
facts.quote: The material recovered consisted of a near-complete skull with its mandible and several bones belonging to the postcranial skeleton

facts.statement: James Kitching was the director of the Evolutionary Studies Institute at the University of the Witwatersrand when he found the fossil.
facts.quote: At the time, Kitching was the director of the Evolutionary Studies Institute (previously the Bernard Price Institute) of the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg

facts.statement: James Kitching and Christopher Gow initially misidentified the fossils as the species Pedeticosaurus leviseuri.
facts.quote: Together Kitching and Gow misidentified this new species of sphenosuchian crocodylomorph and assigned the fossils to an existing crocodylomorph species, Pedeticosaurus leviseuri

facts.statement: Jim Clark and Hans-Dieter Sues re-described the fossils in 2002, identifying them as a new species.
facts.quote: Over a decade later in 2002, two researchers visiting from abroad, Jim Clark and Hans-Dieter Sues, re-described the fossils

facts.statement: Litargosuchus is a monotypic genus, meaning only one species is known.
facts.quote: The Litargosuchus fossil is monotypic and is the only known fossil of this species that has been found to date

facts.statement: The skull material of the holotype specimen has been lost.
facts.quote: The skull material of the Litargosuchus holotype was lost

facts.statement: The remaining parts of the holotype are stored at the Evolutionary Studies Institute.
facts.quote: The remains of the holotype currently remain stored at the Evolutionary Studies Institute

facts.statement: Litargosuchus was a small, gracile crocodylomorph restricted to the Sinemurian stage of the lower Jurassic.
facts.quote: Litargosuchus was a small, gracile non-crocodyliform spheosuchid crocodylomorph restricted to the Sinemurian of the lower Jurassic

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodiles, Litargosuchus was a terrestrial predator capable of running.
facts.quote: Unlike modern crocodiles, Litargosuchus was a cursorial, terrestrial predator

facts.statement: Litargosuchus had unusually elongated limbs, with hind limbs slightly longer than the front ones.
facts.quote: It had unusually elongated limbs with its hind limbs slightly longer than its front

facts.statement: Researchers believe Litargosuchus hunted like a wolf but likely lived a solitary life.
facts.quote: It is thought that Litargosuchus pursued its prey much like a wolf; however, Litargosuchus were likely solitary

facts.statement: Litargosuchus is currently classified within the basal clade Sphenosuchidae.
facts.quote: Litargosuchus is currently positioned within Sphenosuchidae, a basal clade of non-crocodyliform crocodylomorphs

facts.statement: The exact status of Litargosuchus within Sphenosuchia is uncertain due to poor understanding of the group's phylogeny.
facts.quote: However, phylogenetic relationships within the Sphenosuchia are poorly understood so its status within this clade is uncertain

facts.statement: Litargosuchus is accepted as a member of the crown archosaur clade.
facts.quote: However, it is accepted as a member of the greater crown archosaur clade

facts.statement: Litargosuchus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago, from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name Litargosuchus comes from Greek and means 'fast running crocodile'.
rejected.quote: its genus name Litargosuchus is derived from Greek meaning 'fast running crocodile'
